scenes.narration: El truco se llama función de activación.
Sin ella, tu red solo separa con líneas rectas. La activación la deja doblarse y envolver los datos.
Y es real: sin activación la frontera es una raya y falla. Con ReLU se curva y acierta.

ml_demo.code:
import torch, torch.nn as nn
from sklearn.datasets import make_moons
torch.manual_seed(0)
X, y = make_moons(300, noise=0.2, random_state=0)
Xt = torch.tensor(X, dtype=torch.float32); yt = torch.tensor(y, dtype=torch.float32).view(-1,1)
def train(act):
    layers = [nn.Linear(2,16)]
    if act: layers += [nn.ReLU()]
    layers += [nn.Linear(16,1)]
    net = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(net.parameters(), 0.05); lf = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
    for _ in range(400):
        opt.zero_grad(); loss = lf(net(Xt), yt); loss.backward(); opt.step()
    return net
xx, yy = np.meshgrid(np.linspace(-2,3,300), np.linspace(-1.5,2,300))
grid = torch.tensor(np.c_[xx.ravel(), yy.ravel()], dtype=torch.float32)
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1,2, figsize=(9,5.2))
for ax, act, title in [(axs[0], False, 'SIN activacion'), (axs[1], True, 'CON ReLU')]:
    net = train(act)
    with torch.no_grad(): Z = torch.sigmoid(net(grid)).numpy().reshape(xx.shape)
    ax.contourf(xx, yy, Z, levels=12, cmap='magma', alpha=0.7)
    ax.scatter(X[y==0,0], X[y==0,1], c=CYAN, s=14, zorder=3)
    ax.scatter(X[y==1,0], X[y==1,1], c=MAG, s=14, zorder=3)
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
